verses.1: In the second year of Josiah, son of Josias, king of Israel, Amasias, son of Josiah, became king of Judah.
verses.2: He ruled for forty-five years. He also ruled in Jerusalem for forty-nine years. His mother’s name was Yehoadan, who came from Jerusalem.
verses.3: And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, but not like his father David. He did not do everything that his father Joash did.
verses.4: Only the idols remained unbroken. The people continued to worship and offer sacrifices to those idols.
verses.5: And when the queen became stronger in her hands, she defeated her own servants who had served her father.
verses.6: And the children of the murderers were not killed, as it is written in Moses’ law. Jehovah commanded that fathers should not bear responsibility for their sons, and sons should not bear responsibility for their fathers. Only those who commit sin will die.
verses.7: He struck Adam in the Garden of Eden. He took away the tree of life during that battle. And he named it “Yakthael” until today.
verses.8: So, Amziah sent demons to Yehoshua, son of Yehohaz, son of Jehu, king of Israel. He was ordered to say, “Let the faces of those who see this be turned away.”
verses.9: And Joshua, the king of Israel, sent an envoy to Amariah, the king of Judah, with these words: “The girl who is in Bethlehem has sent someone to Erez Bethlehem. Tell her that she can take her daughter as a wife.” Then he went through the land of Bethlehem and brought back the girl.
verses.10: “Listen, you have killed Adam. You should be ashamed of yourself. Return to your house. Why do you continue to do evil? You and Judah will fall together.”
verses.11: And Amasya did not hear this. Then Jehoash became king of Israel. They saw his face, and Amasya became king of Judah in the house of Shemesh, which belonged to Judah.
verses.12: And Judah was attacked before Israel. Then each man went back to his own tent.
verses.13: And Amaziah, king of Judah, son of Jehoash, son of Ahaziah, was defeated by Jehoash, king of Israel. He came into Jerusalem and destroyed the people of Jerusalem at the gate of Ephraim, all the way to the gate of Phinah. It was a destruction of four thousand men.
verses.14: And he took all the gold and silver, as well as all the utensils found in the Temple of Jehovah and in the treasures of the king’s palace. He also took the children of the tribes and appointed them as guards.
verses.15: And the additional words of Jehoash, who did what he did and whose reign lasted for a long time. And what he did in fighting against Amaziah, king of Judah—these are not recorded in the book of the days of the kings of Israel.
verses.16: Jehoshaphat lay down with his ancestors. He was buried in Samaria, along with the kings of Israel. Yerobam, his son, became king after him.
verses.17: Amasya, son of Joash, became king of Judah after the death of Joash, son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel. He ruled for fifteen years.
verses.18: And the additional words of Amasya are not written in the book of the days of the kings of Judah.
verses.19: And they tied him up with ropes in Jerusalem. Then they sent him to Kishah. They sent others after him to Kishah, and he died there.
verses.20: They carried him onto the horses, and he was buried in Jerusalem, with his ancestors, in the city of David.
verses.21: And all the people of Judah took Azariah as their king. He was the son of fourteen years old. They made him king after his father, Amaziah.
verses.22: He built Eilat, and it became a place where people from Judah could settle after the king died along with his ancestors.
verses.23: In the year of fifty-five years after Amasya, son of Joash, king of Judah. In the year of forty-one years after Jeroboam, son of Joash, king of Israel, in Shomron.
verses.24: And he did evil in the eyes of the LORD. He was not spared from all his sins. Jehoshaphat, son of Nebat, who led Israel astray.
verses.25: He restored the boundaries of Israel from the coming of Hamat to the Sea of Ararat, as the Lord God of Israel had commanded through His servant Jonah, son of Amoz, the prophet who came from Gath.
verses.26: For the LORD saw that the poor of Israel were in great distress; they were trapped and left without help. There was no one to save Israel.
verses.27: And the LORD did not speak against the name of Israel from under heaven. Instead, He saved them through Joram son of Josiah.
verses.28: And all the words of Jeroboam, and everything he did, and his reign over Israel—those things are not recorded in the book of the days of the kings of Israel.
verses.29: And Yeravam lay down with his fathers, along with the kings of Israel. Zekherya, his son, became his king.
